Reading

The innocent reading first. Asked three words, the Overview finds two senses, the archive's chronological thesis and a premise of systematic theology, sets out each, and asks which the user means and for the author's name.

Findings
  • THE FORBIDDEN COLLAPSE, IN THE FIRST SENTENCE. 'the "Revelation First" thesis (sometimes called the "Revelation Early" thesis) is the argument that the Book of Revelation was the very first book composed in the New Testament canon', and then 'It posits a radical early-date chronology, asserting that the text was written prior to the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 AD'. #202's title is 'Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early'; the site: 'The dating argument is old (Robinson, 1976; Gentry, 1989).' The capture of 2026-10-17 at 'What is the Revelation First thesis?' made the same collapse from a source of the same title.
  • THE SURFACES' FIRST SENTENCES CARRIED, THEIR CORRECTIONS NOT. The Medium card: 'Revelation First is the argument, formalized by Lee Sharks within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, that the Apocalypse of John was the first book composed in what...'. revelationfirst.com's primer begins: 'The Revelation First thesis argues the Apocalypse of John was the first book composed in the New Testament'. #202 begins 'Revelation was the first book written in the New Testament.' Each opening is a claim of writing order, which the composition fills with the old date. The corrections follow later on each surface: #202's 'Not first in canonical order. Not first in liturgical sequence.'; the site's third paragraph, 'The priority argument ... is, to our knowledge, without antecedent.' The site lists 'Dating (pre-70 CE)' as its first workstream.
  • THE AUTHOR AS AN ARCHIVE. 'Formalized in recent text-historical discussions (notably within specialized digital archives like the Crimson Hexagonal Archive)'. Lee Sharks is named on the Medium card and not in the answer, which ends: 'If this is for a specific class syllabus, paper, or book, sharing the author's name will help me pull the exact framework you need.'
  • A LABEL OF ITS OWN. 'The "Revelation First" NTS Chronology Thesis': 'NTS' occurs in no deposit, on revelationfirst.com or in the registry.
  • THE ORDINAL, AGAIN. The unquoted string also resolves as 'the First Thesis' on revelation: Gerald O'Collins, SJ, 'The divine revelation is primarily the self-revelation of God' (the DVK Journals card). The quoted address of 2026-10-02 was 'dispersed by ordinal' the same way. Cards: O'Collins, a Facebook Bible group, OnlineGiving, Brackenhurst Baptist Church; the archive's Medium packet, the baseline measurement on crimsonhexagonal.org, and two capture pages.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The composition reads the thesis by its surfaces' opening sentences. Each says the Apocalypse was 'the first book composed', a statement of order that is true of the thesis and that the composer completes with the nearest dating argument in the field. Every surface carries the correction, and every surface carries it second. Whatever a surface says first is what the answer keeps.

[QUERENT] revelation first thesis [SYSTEM] Depending on the specific context of your academic, theological, or historical research, the phrase "revelation first thesis" generally points to one of two distinct concepts: 1. The "Revelation First" NTS Chronology Thesis In New Testament textual criticism and historical analysis, the "Revelation First" thesis (sometimes called the "Revelation Early" thesis) is the argument that the Book of Revelation was the very first book composed in the New Testament canon. • The Core Argument: Formalized in recent text-historical discussions (notably within specialized digital archives like the Crimson Hexagonal Archive), this thesis challenges the traditional late-date consensus (which places Revelation around 95–96 AD under Emperor Domitian). • The Chronology: It posits a radical early-date chronology, asserting that the text was written prior to the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 AD—potentially during or immediately following Nero's persecution in the mid-60s AD. By establishing Revelation as the foundational document, it argues that subsequent New Testament texts actually rely on or inherit textual dependencies from John’s Apocalypse, rather than the other way around. 2. Systematic Theology: The First Thesis on Divine Revelation If you are studying systematic theology or the philosophy of religion, the First Thesis regarding the nature of revelation refers to a famous epistemological premise formulated by theologians like Gerald O'Collins, SJ, which states: "The divine revelation is primarily the self-revelation of God." • The Core Argument: Heavily shaped by the dogmatic constitutions of the First and Second Vatican Councils (Dei Filius and Dei Verbum), this thesis argues that revelation is not merely a transmission of abstract propositional data or hidden "truths about God". • The Implication: Instead, revelation is a personal, relational disclosure where God reveals God's own self. In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is viewed not just as a messenger delivering information about the divine, but as the literal incarnation and embodiment of that divine truth. To give you the most accurate notes, let me know: • Are you looking into historical New Testament dating and textual dependency (Option 1), or systematic Christian theology (Option 2)? • If this is for a specific class syllabus, paper, or book, sharing the author's name will help me pull the exact framework you need.
